chapter: Apollo Bar, Apollo managers and Harlem nightlife
title: Managing Johnny Hodges at the Apollo Bar
summary: When Duke toured Europe in 1948, Whaley arranges Johnny Hodges at the Apollo Bar, with Billy Eckstine and Hibbler, and Hodges returns to Duke.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Right, he was a great bass player. You know, in '48 when Duke went to Europe, he didn't take the whole band, see, so I used to go up to the Apollo Bar, that was on 25th Street --

Yeah, and I used to go to the man and say why don't you get some music in here so he says well, who should I get and I said get ahold of Johnny Hodges, so I went down and saw Johnny that night and I said go up to the Apollo bar and talk to the man about business. All right.

Johnny went up, the man hired Johnny and Johnny hired me as a manager and Junior Ragland Ragland was there and I wonder who else was there, anyway, he was one of the spots and Billy Eckstine was the other spot. We had Hibler on our -- singing,
and we opened and you couldn't get in there, man, they talked about Johnny Hodges is at the Apollo bar.
Oh, he was a sensation up there.

Sure, man, you couldn't get in that place and they'd pay $5 a head and Billy -- the second week Billy Eckstine came in and the opening night Billy wanted to quit. I said what's the matter, he said, man, they don't need me here. They got Hibbler and Johnny so finally he stayed but oh, that was a great spot and the man says, how long and I said oh, he'll stay. When Duke come back, Duke come up there and they gave a big party for Duke.
Duke talked to him -- I said to Johnny, you're going to Chicago and the man's going to double your salary. No, Que was the one that made him quit.

Yeah. Que said he got too much honor himself, he can't go. I said, he only had six people and he's making double the money. They were going to give him a whole lot of money up in Chicago and no, Johnny went back to Duke. I said, well, that's the end of that.
